plugin-data.name: Nova Companion
plugin-data.description: Companion plugin for the Nova theme.

jdpc-section-sidebar-subtitle:
Three widgets that render in your sidebar, in this order: Categories → Latest Posts → About.

Latest Posts and About will also render in the footer aside.
jdpc-section-external-subtitle: Behavior for anchors that point outside your own domain in post/page content.
jdpc-section-feeds-subtitle: Machine-readable feeds for RSS readers, search engines, and sitemap consumers. Both files are regenerated automatically whenever you create, edit, or delete a page (and whenever you save these settings).
jdpc-rss-items-tip: How many of your most recent pages appear in the feed.
jdpc-section-social-subtitle: Meta tags consumed by social platforms when someone shares one of your URLs — Open Graph (Facebook, LinkedIn, Discord, Slack, Mastodon, iMessage) and Twitter/X Card (the legacy twitter:* tags that X still honors and falls back to OG for the rest). Both render in the page <head>.
jdpc-og-default-image-tip: Fallback image used on the home page and anywhere a specific page has no cover image. Use the relative path to an image on your site or an absolute URL to an external image.
jdpc-og-fb-appid-tip: Optional. Emits <meta property="fb:app_id">; only relevant if you use Facebook Insights / Login on this domain. Leave blank to skip.
jdpc-twitter-card-type-tip: Large image cards get noticeably better engagement. Choose Summary if you typically don't have a cover image.
jdpc-twitter-site-tip: Optional. Emits <meta name="twitter:site"> so cards attribute back to your handle. Include the leading @ or leave blank to skip.
jdpc-twitter-default-image-tip: Fallback image used when a specific page has no cover image. Use the relative path to an image on your site or an absolute URL to an external image.
jdpc-section-stats-subtitle: Inject an analytics or web-stats snippet at body end on every page.
jdpc-section-easymde-subtitle: Replaces the default page editor on the create-page and edit-page admin views with EasyMDE — a richer markdown editor with a toolbar, side-by-side preview, fullscreen, and an optional spell checker. The editor is only loaded on those two views, so other admin pages are unaffected.
jdpc-easymde-tabsize-tip: Number of spaces a Tab keystroke inserts in the editor.
jdpc-easymde-toolbar-tip: Comma-separated list of toolbar items, each in double quotes. Use "|" for a separator. Reference: EasyMDE toolbar icons.
jdpc-section-version-subtitle: The version chip in the admin sidebar that polls version.bludit.com for newer releases.
jdpc-section-html-subtitle: Inject raw HTML at specific points in the page. Common uses: verification meta tags (Search Console, Mastodon, IndieAuth), custom fonts or analytics that don't fit the Web stats section, third-party chat widgets, schema.org JSON-LD, or experimental scripts. Anything pasted here is emitted verbatim on every page in its area — be deliberate about what you put in.
jdpc-html-head-tip: Emitted inside the <head> tag on every public page. Use for meta tags, link rel=preconnect, JSON-LD, fonts, etc.
jdpc-html-bodybegin-tip: Emitted immediately after <body> on every public page. Use for noscript fallbacks or skip-to-content content that needs to be the first thing in the body.
jdpc-html-bodyend-tip: Emitted just before </body> on every public page. Use for third-party widgets or scripts that should load after the rest of the page.
jdpc-html-adminhead-tip: Emitted inside the <head> tag of every admin page. Generally only useful for custom admin styling.
jdpc-html-adminbodybegin-tip: Emitted immediately after <body> on every admin page.
jdpc-html-adminbodyend-tip: Emitted just before </body> on every admin page.
jdpc-section-staticgen-subtitle: Generate a fully static HTML copy of the site to bl-content/static-build/. Useful for archiving, mirroring, or hosting the site without PHP.
sgj-section-action-subtitle: Renders every public URL, copies referenced assets, rewrites links to document-relative paths, and writes the result to bl-content/static-build/. The admin area, drafts, and the bl-content databases are never included.
sgj-confirm-body: This will render every public page and overwrite anything currently in bl-content/static-build/. The build runs synchronously — keep this tab open until it finishes.
sgj-loading-body: Rendering pages and copying assets. Please don’t close this tab — the page will refresh automatically when the build finishes.
sgj-production-url-tip: Optional. Public URL the static build will be served from, e.g. https://example.com. When set, this overrides the site URL during the build: $_SERVER is faked to match (so plugins that branch on SERVER_PORT / HTTPS / HTTP_HOST — like the web-stats dev-port check — see production values), and Open Graph / Twitter / canonical URLs are re-absolutized against this host. Leave blank to use the site URL from Settings → Advanced.
sgj-exclude-paths-tip: One path per line. Any URL whose path starts with one of these is skipped (admin and bl-content/databases are always skipped).
sgj-extra-dirs-tip: One directory name per line. Each must live at the site root (next to bl-content) — e.g. resume, dumbprojects. Its contents are copied verbatim into the build with no rewriting, and the directory is auto-excluded from the crawl so Bludit doesn't try to render it. Use this for stand-alone HTML directories that aren't part of Bludit's pages. Flat names only (no slashes, no ..); dotfiles are skipped.
sgj-build-locked: Another build appears to be in progress. If this is wrong, remove the lock file from the workspace and try again.
sgj-build-no-output-dir: Could not create the output directory.
sgj-howitworks-1: Pages are rendered in-process by Bludit itself — the plugin does not make any HTTP requests, so the build works the same way locally, inside Vagrant, and in production.
sgj-howitworks-2: HTML pages are written as path/index.html so clean URLs keep working; all absolute and root-relative links are rewritten to document-relative paths.
sgj-howitworks-3: Referenced theme, upload, and other public assets are copied verbatim from disk; anything under the admin URI or bl-content/databases is always skipped.
sgj-howitworks-4: Drafts, scheduled pages, and any path you list under Exclude paths are never written to the build.
sgj-howitworks-5: A 404.html is written to the build root using Bludit's configured Page not found. Static hosts like GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Render and Surge serve it automatically. For Apache, add ErrorDocument 404 /404.html to .htaccess. For nginx, add error_page 404 /404.html; to the server block.
jdpc-enable-external-target-blank: Open external links in a new tab
jdpc-enable-version-check: Show the version chip in the admin sidebar
jdpc-dev-port-tip: If the request comes in on this port, the web stats snippet below is NOT emitted. Use this if you run a local copy of this admin (a dev mirror, a staging instance, or anything else that isn't production) on a specific port — without it, your own development traffic would show up in the production analytics and skew the numbers. Leave blank to always emit.
jdpc-stats-code-tip: Pasted verbatim into the body end on every page. Used for Statcounter / Plausible / similar.
jdpc-howitworks-external: A static page whose Description field is set to external:https://somedomain.com will open the URL after the : and render with target="_blank" rel="noopener" in the About widget and in the theme's footer aside. Static pages with the external URL set will also not show in search results.
jdpc-howitworks-404: A static page whose Description field is set to 404 is hidden from the About widget, the theme's footer aside, site navigation, and search. The page is still served at its URL — it just stops appearing in navigation and search. Set the Description to 404 on the static page that you want to serve as your site's not-found page.
jdpc-howitworks-archived: The Categories widget always sorts a category literally named Archived to the bottom of the list, regardless of alphabetical order. Posts that are in the Archived category will have an "archived" banner at the top of the page content and will not show in search results or in the site navigation.
jdpc-howitworks-targetblank: The 'open external links in new tab' setting injects a small script at body-end that walks every <a> on the rendered page and, for hosts that do not match the current one, sets target="_blank" and ensures rel includes noopener noreferrer (to prevent reverse-tabnabbing). Theme-rendered external anchors already include rel="noopener" inline; this script handles links inside post content.
